text:
incident-bot: PAGER: billing-metering detected delayed emits from usage-collector (12:05-12:15 UTC). Metric: emit-window-gap > threshold. Token delta drift ~+25% vs baseline. Affected shard: eu-west-1. Runbook: <https://redwood/runbooks/metering-emit-gap>. Paging billing-oncall.

nina (oncall-billing): ack — looking. pulling live dashboard now.

nina (oncall-billing): quick query: `select count(*) from emits where region='eu-west-1' and ts > now() - interval '30 minutes'` shows a 40% drop vs usual. queue.backlog for usage-emitter-service jumped from 200 -> 4.2k.

liam (eng-runtime): thanks. I see a deploy of batching/kv-window v2 at 11:48 from canary. Could be a batching regression. tagging @ben @dave.

ben (billing): customer-facing overage flagging is wired to this stream for a subset of customers. If counts are low, some customers may see late reports and temporary overage triggers when delayed emits replay. We should consider muting overage alerts for eu-west slices until resolved.

dave (sre): tailing emitter logs now. `kubectl -n billing logs -l app=usage-emitter -c emitter --since=30m` shows intermittent 502s to kafka-proxy and a steady reconnect loop from emitter-worker-7.

nina (oncall-billing): confirmed: emitter-worker-7 heartbeat missing since 12:06. Attempting a soft restart: `k rollout restart deployment/usage-emitter-worker -n billing --field-selector=metadata.name=emitter-worker-7`

liam (eng-runtime): rolling back batching/kv-window to v1 on canary; if that clears backlog we plan a full rollback. Command: `deploy rollback usage-emitter --to-version v1-kvwindow` — proceeding.

ben (billing): I'm going to open a temporary suppression rule for overage-alerts for customers with tag `eu-west-affected` to avoid noisy alerts. Will ping ops when done.

maya (customer-success): FYI: got an inbound from a mid-market customer about an invoice "usage anomaly" email at 12:10. I'll hold customer comms until we know impact. Can you confirm whether invoice calc uses resolved window or raw stream?

liam (eng-runtime): invoice pipeline reads reconciled ledger, so immediate invoice should be unaffected long-term, but temporary alerting can happen from upstream flags.

nina (oncall-billing): restart outcome: emitter-worker-7 restarted, but backlog still climbing. Rolling back completed on canary at 12:28 — `deploy status` shows v1 active on 2 canaries.

dave (sre): after rollback I see emit rate returning to baseline. backlog drain rate increased, error 502s disappeared. tails show normal commit frequency.

incident-bot: Automated check: token-delta drift reduced to +3% vs baseline; emit-window-gap cleared in eu-west-1.

nina (oncall-billing): confirmed counts normalized across last 10m. disabling suppression for overage-alerts in 10m to verify no false positives.

ben (billing): suppression in place now. I'll keep it for 30m and then re-evaluate.

maya (customer-success): I'm sending a short note to the affected customer saying we're investigating transient telemetry and will follow up if there's billing impact. Draft: "We detected a transient telemetry delay affecting usage reporting in EU region between 12:05–12:25 UTC. We're mitigating now — no confirmed billing impact; we'll update after reconciliation."

liam (eng-runtime): leaving follow-ups: (1) root-cause triage on batching change and kafka-proxy 502s, (2) improve emitter-worker heartbeat alerting to detect missing heartbeats faster, (3) add a short-circuit to mute overage triggers when backlog > X.

nina (oncall-billing): handing off to liam for post-incident owner. I'll mark this as resolved for oncall and add notes to the runbook. assigning follow-up ticket: RH-1842.

liam (eng-runtime): taking postmortem ownership. will schedule a 30-min incident review and include billing, sre, and cs. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria (observer-bot): Incident resolved by rollback + restart. Timeline logged.

nina (oncall-billing): closing pager. If any late reconciliations surface overnight, tag #billing-ops.
